title: AI-guided experiments establish feasible 500–950 W printing configurations for GRCop-42
summary: A closed-loop Bayesian experimental-design method, BEAM, found multiple defect-free directed-energy-deposition configurations for GRCop-42 copper alloy at infrared laser powers from 950 down to 500 W. Researchers report that these experimentally successful settings solved a process-development problem that had resisted several months of manual trials, enabling GRCop-42 fabrication on lower-power platforms. This is a manufacturing-process result for an existing alloy, not a new alloy composition.
ai_technology: BEAM (Bayesian Experimental design for Additive Manufacturing)

evidence.tested: A closed-loop Bayesian experimental-design method, BEAM, found multiple defect-free directed-energy-deposition configurations for GRCop-42 copper alloy at infrared laser powers from 950 down to 500 W.
evidence.unknown: The paper establishes feasible configurations in one directed-energy-deposition system for one alloy. It does not demonstrate aerospace-qualified components, service life or broader transfer to other machines and alloys. The reported defect-free characterization is bounded to the study's print assessment.
evidence.ai_role: BEAM uses a probabilistic surrogate and adaptive experimental-design strategy to select small batches of process configurations for laboratory testing; print outcomes update its feasibility model and guide subsequent tests. The loop identified successful configurations at 950, 700, 600 and 500 W, where prior manual trials had failed for months.
